decisions.reason: The whole-run conclusion in proof 2.1 omits deterministic prime search. The supplied search tests up to N squared candidate/divisor pairs; its established cost is O(N^2 log^2 N), not part of the O((TD+L) log^2 p) round/evaluation count. Claim 4 now retains that latter component and explicitly adds the search cost, including constant setup at T=0. This is a logical accounting gap in the asserted total bound, not a missing citation.

The final sentence of the Statement overclaims gap monotonicity. One vertex with an empty-relation ordinary loop is 2-regular in the slot convention. At t=1, all three positions are tested, any move violates, and the all-hold probability is (1/2)^3=1/8 independently of the view. Thus UNSAT falls from 1 to 7/8. The repair preserves the entire perfect-completeness contract and distinguishes it from the separate conditional small-gap estimate; the counterexample is recorded explicitly.

reviews.reason: Checked the T=n(n+3)/2 operator schedule, D+1 fixed-width coefficients, at most T residue challenges and Tk coins, three Horner evaluations per passed round, and O(L) terminal circuit evaluation. Claim 4 and steps 2.1 and 3.1 now add the existing deterministic prime-search bound O(N^2 log^2 N); T=0 has p=3, no messages and constant setup. This is the adjudicator author check of this repair, not an independent review of it.

Finite nonempty alphabet and finite vertex set ensure a maximizing base labeling exists. Its endpoint-defined canonical views read exactly the two base labels at each tested move, so all relations pass, including loops; holds impose no test. The hold^t-edge-hold^t argument in Remarks also proves the stated perfect-satisfiability converse by self-coordinate decoding. The repaired Statement preserves this completeness result and no longer asserts the false monotonicity inequality. This author check does not constitute independent review of the repair.

interface_changes.before_clause: Hence the whole run costs $O\!\left(TD\log^2p+L\log^2p\right)$ bit operations for the rounds and the terminal step.
interface_changes.after_clause: The rounds and the terminal step together cost $O\!\left((TD+L)\log^2p\right)$ bit operations. Including the deterministic prime search, the verifier's total cost is $O\!\left(N^2\log^2N+(TD+L)\log^2p\right)$ bit operations, still polynomial in the input length; when $T=0$, setting $p=3$ costs only constant time.
